question.explanation:
The roots of $g(z)$ are the solutions to the equation $g(z) = 0.$ In our case, we have

\[ \dfrac{z^3 + 5z^2 - z - 5}{z^3 + 6z^2 + 5z} = 0. \]

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} g(z)&=\dfrac{z^3 + 5z^2 - z - 5}{z^3 + 6z^2 + 5z} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{z^2(z + 5) - (z + 5)}{z(z^2 + 6z + 5)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(z^2 - 1)(z + 5)}{z(z +1)(z + 5)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(z + 1)(z - 1)(z + 5)}{z(z +1)(z + 5)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(z - 1)\cancel{(z + 1)(z + 5)}}{z\cancel{(z + 1)(z + 5)}} & \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{z -1}{z} \end{align*}

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $z\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} z - 1 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad z = 1 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution to $g(z) = 0$ is $z=1.$

question.explanation:
First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} f(u)&=\dfrac{6u^2 + 6u - 36}{3u^2 + 9u} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{6(u^2 + u - 6)}{3u(u + 3)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{6(u +3)(u - 2)}{3u(u + 3)}\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{2\cdot\cancel{3(u +3)}(u - 2)}{u \cdot \cancel{3(u + 3)}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(u-2)}{u} \end{align}

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $u\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2(u - 2) &= 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u = 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to $f(u)=0$ is $u=2.$

example.title: Finding the Roots of a Rational Function With Common Factors

question.explanation:
The roots of $f(h)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(h) = 0.$ In our case, we have

\[ \dfrac{3h^2 + 18}{h^2 + 10h +25} = 0. \]

First, we factor $f(h),$ as follows: \begin{align*} f(h) &= \dfrac{3h^2 + 18}{h^2 + 10h + 25}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3(h^2 + 6)}{(h+5)^2} \end{align*}

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $h\mathbin{:}$

\[ 3(h^2 + 6)=0 \]

Since $h^2 + 6 \gt 0$ for all $h,$ there is no real solution to $f(h)=0.$ Therefore, $f(h)$ has no real roots.
